rules_review: The full official face agrees with the accepted single printing: Chaos Unit, 2 Energy, 0 Power, 2 Might, Yordle/Bandle City. The Assault keyword is granted, not intrinsic.
Core 204.1.c, 383.2-3 and 403-407 distinguish the optional 1 Energy play cost from the triggered ability base cost. Banish happens before responses; Assault is granted only on resolution.

Core 355.10.c: the trash card pays a cost and is not targeted. The sole unit target may be friendly, enemy or Gust Monk itself. Enemy Deflect is an additional ability cost and cannot use spell-only Power.
Core 405.2 permits declining the banish cost, including empty trashes. Direct and staged Add actions are undone without undoing the completed unit play or refunding its optional Energy.

An announced trash cost remains pinned to its physical copy during staged payment. Earlier removals adjust its index; removal of that copy or burnout cannot substitute a later identical card. Undo restores the payment boundary.
A counter or departed last target does not refund the paid banish cost. Removal of Gust Monk itself does not stop a finalized ability targeting another unit.
Assault 2 adds Might only while attacking, stacks with other grants and expires at turn cleanup. Hunters Circle discounts the total without erasing the paid-optional-cost condition.
Irelia Fervent receives the choose and ready interactions through Irelia Blade Dancer after costs are paid. These interactions are independently exercised by focused tests.
The API exposes an explicit resolve_trigger_trash_payment action and public non-target cost candidates, with read-only validation and quotes and atomic rejection of invalid or stale actions.

Beginner and Advanced advice use visible state. Normal and small native click tests cover optional Energy, selecting the unit, inspecting both trash choices, paying the banish cost, resolution and declining when empty.
findings_resolved: Initial focused fixtures used the wrong location for spell-only Power and an incorrect legend for an Irelia-ready expectation. The fixtures were corrected before the final focused and full suites.
The initial full-suite compile found a smoke assertion that required an unavailable Debug implementation. Its equivalent equality assertion compiled; the subsequent complete 104-harness run passed.
The complete-game observer now detects stored temporary Assault grants directly instead of counting any unit with Assault.
limitations: This adds Gust Monk to custom decks, not a sixth tournament preset. The now-verified Arito list still needs preset integration and exact-list match testing.

The 24-game API campaign observed seven opponent-trash costs and five declines. Both own-trash and opponent-trash payments are covered by focused rules/API tests; no own-trash payment is claimed for that campaign.
Native acceptance uses x86-64 Linux. The latest separate Nix acceptance remains Back Off source 6411bd141a3bff35eb6491e2a6202496045030bf, recorded in irelia_backoff_nix.json.
The accepted dated card catalog remains in use while duplicate live publisher printing IDs are unresolved. The current rules and errata check is not a fresh full-gallery acceptance.
Full Standard parity, all legal cards, individual combat attribution, best-of-three sideboarding and tournament-strength AI remain unfinished.
